speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are a child presenting with frequent nosebleeds, bleeding from your mucous membranes, and small red spots on your skin called petechiae. To understand what is causing this, I need to ask you some questions about your medical history. Have you or your family ever been told you have a bleeding disorder like hemophilia or von Willebrand disease?

speaker: Patient
text: 4-year-old male. The child's parent reports that the child has been experiencing frequent episodes of nosebleeds and has had several instances of bleeding from the gums. Additionally, there have been occurrences of unexplained bruising and petechiae, primarily on the distal extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text: Yes, your parent has confirmed frequent nosebleeds, gum bleeding, unexplained bruising, and petechiae on the arms and legs. Given these symptoms involving both mucous membranes and the skin, I need to check your platelet count; can I see the results of a Complete Blood Count (CBC)? REQUEST TEST: CBC

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Frequent epistaxis. I also have Mucous membrane bleeding, Diffuse petechiae on distal extremities.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical issues. Up-to-date on vaccinations. Social history: Attends preschool. Lives with parents and one older sibling.

speaker: Patient
text: Denies any fever, significant weight loss, joint pains, or recent infections. This is only for study purposes, so you do not need to list warnings or many alternatives. Please just provide the best final answer.

speaker: Doctor
text: The child denies fever, weight loss, joint pain, or recent infections. To evaluate the platelets and coagulation factors, please provide the results of the CBC and Coagulation Panel (PT/INR, PTT). REQUEST TEST: CBC; REQUEST TEST: Coagulation_Panel

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: CBC: WBC 6,500 /μL; Hemoglobin 12.1 g/dL; Platelets 280,000 /μL (normal). Coagulation_Panel: PT 12 seconds (normal); aPTT 30 seconds (normal). Special_Test: ELISA_Binding_Assay Findings: Platelet surfaces deficient in GIIb/IIIa receptors.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Bernard-Soulier Syndrome. The clinical presentation of mucosal bleeding and petechiae, combined with normal CBC and coagulation studies, alongside the specific finding of a deficiency in GpIIb/IIIa receptors, confirms this rare platelet function disorder.
